html:
The Battle of the Allia was fought about 387 BCE (Roman tradition says 390 BCE) where the little Allia stream meets the Tiber, eleven Roman miles north of Rome. The Senones, a Celtic people from northern Italy led by Brennus, routed the army of the Roman Republic and then sacked the city.

Many Romans fled to Veii. In Rome only the Capitol held out. Later stories say the sacred geese of Juno woke the defenders when the Gauls tried a night attack. The Gauls finally left after being paid a ransom in gold. When the Romans complained that the weights were rigged, Brennus is said to have thrown his sword on the scales and said "Vae victis", "woe to the conquered". Roman writers later claimed that Camillus arrived in time to win the gold back, which most historians doubt.

The sack scarred Roman memory. The day of the defeat, 18 July, became an unlucky day in the calendar, and fear of Gauls lasted for centuries. Soon afterwards Rome built the stone Servian Wall around the city. The story is told at length in Livy's history.
